components.css: .ds-card { min-width: 0; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); background: var(--surface); transition: transform 180ms ease, box-shadow 180ms ease, border-color 180ms ease; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: var(--ink); transform: translateY(-3px); box-shadow: var(--shadow); } .ds-card-preview { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: grid; place-items: center; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); color: var(--preview-muted); background: var(--preview-surface); font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-card-body { padding: 22px; } .ds-card-meta { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 10px; margin: 0 0 18px; color: var(--green); font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-card h3 { margin: 0 0 12px; color: var(--ink); font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 1.42rem; letter-spacing: -0.04em; } .ds-card p:not(.ds-card-meta) { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.92rem; line-height: 1.55; } .ds-card a { color: var(--ink); text-underline-offset: 4px; } .ds-card a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--orange); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: BLUE GOLD BLUE Route Board
components.description: Scoped proof sequence showing save, gate, change, and restore in order.
components.html:
1. BLUESave your stuff.Discover, protect, and verify first.
  2. SAFETY GATEProof before change.Unknown or unsafe means stop.
  3. GOLDStart your new computer.Only after BLUE is verified.
  4. BLUEBring your stuff home.Restore what is supported and report the rest.

BLUE BEFORE GOLD. ALWAYS.
components.css: .ds-route-board { padding: 24px; color: #f4f8fa; background: #102733; box-shadow: 0 20px 48px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.18); } .ds-route-board ol { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; } .ds-route-board li { position: relative; min-height: 104px; padding: 16px 18px 18px 72px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(244, 248, 250, 0.2); } .ds-route-board li::before { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 22px; left: 18px; width: 30px; height: 30px; border: 2px solid currentcolor; border-radius: 50%; background: #102733; } .ds-route-board li::after { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 52px; bottom: -23px; left: 33px; width: 2px; background: rgba(244, 248, 250, 0.35); } .ds-route-board li:last-child { border-bottom: 0; } .ds-route-board li:last-child::after { display: none; } .ds-route-board li > span { display: block; margin-bottom: 4px; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.1em; } .ds-route-board li strong { display: block; font-size: 1.12rem; } .ds-route-board li small { display: block; margin-top: 2px; color: #c7d5db; font-size: 0.86rem; } .ds-route-board .ds-route-blue { color: #70c3e9; } .ds-route-board .ds-route-gold { color: #f5c862; } .ds-route-board .ds-route-gate { color: #ffffff; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04); } .ds-route-board > p { margin: 20px 0 0; padding: 14px 18px; color: #102733; background: #e1a51d; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-align: center; }

narrative.overview:
The OMA portfolio is a restrained evidence workshop: engineered, calm, legible, and candid. It presents source-backed work in a light, paper-like field with strong typographic structure, deliberate rules, and dark structural panels when a sequence or proof state needs to hold attention. The interface is typography-led rather than illustration-led. Hierarchy comes from scale, whitespace, aligned rails, and rare functional color.

The shared portfolio surface is the default visual authority for the catalog and supporting pages. The Beacon Wakes, Perception, and BLUE GOLD BLUE surfaces can establish their own scoped palettes and signature compositions while retaining the same discipline of readable type, explicit state, and honest unfinished status. BLUE GOLD BLUE uses blue for protection and information, then reserves gold for its safety-gated change step.
keyCharacteristics: Typography-led hierarchy with JetBrains Mono headings and labels.
IBM Plex Sans body copy with generous readable line lengths.
Light canvas, thin rules, square forms, and dark structural panels.
Functional accents used sparingly to communicate state, action, or attention.

rules.name: The Rare Accent Rule
rules.body: Color is a functional signal. Use an accent to identify an action, state, route, or exception, and let the surrounding light field and dark structure carry the rest of the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Instrument Label Rule
rules.body: Use the mono face for operational language and state. Do not turn body paragraphs into labels or use display scale where a compact status marker is clearer.

rules.name: The Structural Depth Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with surface tone, rules, and whitespace first. A shadow is a state or signature treatment, not a default decoration.

dos: Do lead with the evidence, sequence, or status the visitor needs to understand.
Do use JetBrains Mono for operational labels and IBM Plex Sans for explanatory copy.
Do use whitespace, thin rules, and dark structural panels to create hierarchy before reaching for color.
Do keep interactive targets at least 44px high and preserve visible keyboard focus.
Do scope product palettes to their product surface. On BLUE GOLD BLUE, use blue for protection and information and gold for safety-gated change.
Do make unfinished, under-review, and unknown states explicit in both copy and visual treatment.
donts: Don't replace evidence with fabricated renders, testimonials, prices, countdowns, availability claims, or endorsement language.
Don't introduce illustration-led decoration where typography and structure already communicate the idea.
Don't use rounded cards, pill controls, soft generic gradients, or ornamental shadows that are absent from the incumbent system.
Don't turn the BLUE GOLD BLUE blue and gold semantics into a portfolio-wide color requirement.
Don't use a bright accent as a large decorative wash when a rule, label, or state marker will communicate the same information.
